patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Nextiva and respond.io share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Nextiva and respond.io share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits. Choose Nextiva only if your buying job matches “SMB-friendly unified business communications — Core $15, Engage $25, Scale $75 per user/mo” rather than respond.io's shape. Choose respond.io only if your buying job matches “Omnichannel customer messaging platform (WhatsApp + other channels) with shared inbox and ” rather than Nextiva's shape. Workflow advantage: Nextiva leans business-phone, team-communication; respond.io leans whatsapp-support. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Nextiva and respond.io share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Nextiva is SMB-friendly unified business communications — Core $15, Engage $25, Scale $75 per user/month annual, with messaging apps including WhatsApp; respond.io is Omnichannel customer messaging platform (WhatsApp + other channels) with shared inbox and AI — Starter from $79/month annual-equivalent..
- Company-size focus: Nextiva (micro, small-business, mid-market) vs respond.io (small-business, mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: Nextiva-leaning business-phone, team-communication, contact-center vs respond.io-leaning whatsapp-support.
- Researched limits: Nextiva — Call recording is an add-on on Core rather than included; respond.io — Not a business phone system — no IVR, queues or PSTN calling product.

Limitations — Nextiva: Call recording is an add-on on Core rather than included; Analytics and AI assistance require Scale / higher plans or XBert add-on from $99/mo; respond.io: Not a business phone system — no IVR, queues or PSTN calling product; Platform subscription plus channel/Meta messaging fees create two-layer TCO.
